INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource Development,
having been authorised by the Committee, present this Hundred Eighty First Report of the Committee on the Rajiv
Gandhi University Bill, 2006.
2.         In pursuance of Rule 270 relating to the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees, the Chairman,
Rajya Sabha, referred the Rajiv Gandhi University Bill 2006, as introduced in the Rajya Sabha on the 31
st July, 2006
and pending therein, to the Committee on the 4th August, 2006 for examination and report.
3.         The Committee considered the Bill in two sittings held on the 8th September and the 18th September, 2006.
4.         On the 18 th September 2006, the Committee heard the Secretary, Department of Secondary and Higher
Education on the Rajiv Gandhi University Bill, 2006.  The Committee also took up clause-by-clause consideration of
the Bill and adopted the draft report with amendments in clauses 2(d), 2(e), 6(ix), 6(xix), 22(1), 23(2), 24(2), 25(2), 26,
27, 31(1)(i), 31(1)(k), 36(3), 40, 43 and 47 of the Principal Act and clauses 2(1), 2(2), 9, 17, 18(2), 30(1) and 40(1) of
the Statutes.

REPORT
The Rajiv Gandhi University Bill, 2006 seeks to convert the existing Rajiv Gandhi University, Itanagar, into a Central
University with a view to cater to the needs and aspirations of the people of the State and to minimize the imbalance in
educational facilities in the North Eastern Region.
2.         The Rajiv Gandhi University was established at Itanagar in 1984, under the Rajiv Gandhi University Act, 1984
enacted by the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly. 
3.According to the Department of Secondary and Higher Education, the Arunachal Pradesh government, with its limited
resources, is not in a position to provide adequate funding for development of the Rajiv Gandhi University.  Besides,
existence of a good number of central universities in other States of the region, viz., at Kohima, Silchar, Tezpur, Aizawl,
Imphal and Shillong has caused a huge imbalance in educational facilities within the region, and a consequent migration
of teachers, students and researchers in search of better infrastructural and academic facilities to other States.  There has,
therefore, been persistent demand for conversion of the Rajiv Gandhi University into a central university.   
4.         The Committee was informed that the University Grants Commission (UGC) had constituted a Committee to
consider the issue of conversion of Rajiv Gandhi University into a central university and to estimate the quantum of
funds required for up-gradation of its existing facilities and staff.  The UGC Committee visited the University and had
detailed discussions with the authorities/officers of the State government, the Vice-Chancellor, teaching and non-
teaching employees as well as the students of the University.  The Committee after taking stock of the existing
infrastructure, recommended conversion of the Rajiv Gandhi University into a full-fledged central university through an
Act of Parliament. 
5.         Accordingly, the Rajiv Gandhi University Bill 2006, was introduced in the Rajya Sabha for the establishment
and incorporation of Rajiv Gandhi University as a central university and for repealing of the existing Rajiv Gandhi
University Act, 1984, enacted by the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly. 
6.         The salient features of the aforesaid Bill are as under:-
The Bill seeks to establish and incorporate the existing Rajiv Gandhi University, a state university of Arunachal
Pradesh, under the proposed Central Act by the same name of 'Rajiv Gandhi University' with perpetual succession and
common seal and to provide for the matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
 
The University would be a teaching and affiliating university with its Headquarters at Itanagar and territorial jurisdiction
extending to the whole of the State of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
It would function broadly on the pattern of the existing central universities, particularly of those of the North-Eastern
region.
All Colleges, Institutions, Faculties and Departments affiliated to, or admitted to the privileges of, or maintained by the
existing Rajiv Gandhi University shall stand affiliated to, or admitted to the privilege of, or maintained by the
University.
The annual accounts of the University shall be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and shall be
laid before both Houses of Parliament along with the audit report and the annual report of the University.
During the transitional period, the appointment of the first Officers and the constitution of the first Authorities of the
University would be made by the Visitor for specified terms.
7.         The Committee after going through all the papers and documents and hearing the Secretary, Department of

Secondary and Higher Education, took up clause-by-clause consideration of the Bill.   It suggested the following
amendments/additions to various clauses of the Bill.
Clause 2 (d) and 2 (e)
8.         The Committee notes that the definitions for ‘Approved Institution’ and ‘Approved Teachers’ provided in 2(d)
and 2(e) on page 2 are not explicit and leave some scope for confusion. On a specific query in this regard, the
Committee was informed that the basis for inclusion of these two definitions in the Bill was the existing provision under
the State University Act.  It was clarified that due to lack of higher educational institutions in the State, some institutions
in the State were approved for grant of certificate and diploma courses.  It was envisaged to continue with the existing
facilities till the time higher educational institutions were made operational.  The Committee is, however, not convinced
by the justification given by the Department.  With the State University getting the status of Central University, any
institution existing anywhere can get the approved status.  The Committee, therefore, is of the view that there is need to
amplify the definitions of the terms `Approved Institution’ and ‘Approved Teachers’ with a view to removing possible
ambiguities in these regards. The Committee, therefore, recommends that necessary amendments should be brought in
the relevant provision of the Bill for this purpose. 
Clause 6(ix)
9.1       Clause 6(ix), page 4, provides that the University shall have the power ‘to appoint persons working in any other
University or organization as teachers of the University for a specified period.’
9.2       The Committee is of the considered opinion that the word ‘organization’ in this clause leaves some scope for
different interpretations. The Department clarified that the word ‘organization’ generally meant ‘a teaching or a research
institution, other than a university’.  The Committee feels that this needs to be specified in the Bill with a view to
remove any ambiguity about the nature of the organization.
Clause 6(xix)
10.1     Clause 6(xix), page 5, provides that the University shall have the powers ‘to confer autonomous status on a
College or an Institution or a Department, as the case may be, in accordance with the Statutes.’
10.2     The Committee feels that the provision of the clause amounts to giving unbridled powers to the University for
conferring autonomous status on a College, an Institution or a Department.  The Committee is of the opinion that some
kind of requirements and conditions necessary for making any institution autonomous may be specified.  The
Committee, therefore, recommends that Clause 6(xix) may be suitably amended. 
Clause 22 (1)
 
11.1     Clause 22(1), page 8, provides that the constitution of the Court and the term of office of its members shall be
prescribed by the Statutes.  The Committee however, notes that the Statutes appended to the Bill do not provide for the
constitution of the Court as well as the term of office of its members. 
11.2     The Committee feels that the Court being the apex body of the university, provision for its constitution and term
of office of its members be provided in the first statutes itself.
Clauses 23(2), 24(2), 25(2), 26 and 27
12.1     Clause 23(2), page 8, provides that the constitution of the Executive Council, the term of office of its members
and its powers and functions shall be prescribed by the Statutes.
12.2     Clause 24(2), page 9, provides that the constitution of the Academic Council, the term of office of its members
and its powers and functions shall be prescribed by the Statutes.
12.3     Clause 25(2), page 9, provides that the constitution of the College Development Council, the term of office of its
members and its powers and functions shall be prescribed by the Statutes.
12.4     Clause 26, page 9, provides that the constitution, powers and functions of the Board of Studies shall be
prescribed by the Statutes.
12.5     Clause 27, page 9, provides that the constitution, powers and functions of the Finance Committee shall be
prescribed by the Statutes.
12.6     The Committee notes that the Executive Council, Academic Council, College Development Council, Board of
Studies and Finance Committee are the important decision-making bodies of the University.  The Statutes appended to
the Bill contain provisions only about the powers and functions of these bodies but is silent about their constitution and
term of office.
 
12.7     The Committee, therefore, recommends that the provisions for the constitution and term of office of the
Executive Council, Academic Council,  College Development Council, Board of Studies and Finance Committee, also
be included within corpus of the first Statutes itself.

Clause 31(1)(i) 
13.       Clause 31 deals with power to make Ordinances. The Committee finds that sub-clause (i) on page 11 provides
for making special arrangements “for residence, discipline and teaching of women students.”  The Committee is of the
considered opinion that while this is valid in terms of residence and specific courses for women students, the word
‘discipline’ in this clause appears to be discriminatory; hence unnecessary.  Accordingly, the Committee recommends
that the word ‘discipline’ be deleted from clause 31(1)(i), page 11 of the Bill.
Clause 31(1)(k)
14.       This Clause provides for cooperation and collaboration by the proposed University with other universities,
institutions and other agencies. The Committee feels that the word ‘other agencies’ leaves ample scope for associating
with agencies which might be private and for profit.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the words ‘not for
profit’ may be appropriately added in page 11, line 8 of Clause 31 (1) (k).
Clause 36(3)
15.1     Clause 36(3), page 12, provides that the decision of the Tribunal, in respect of any dispute arising out of the
contract between the University and an employee, shall be final and no suit shall lie in any civil court in respect of the
matters decided by the Tribunal.
15.2     The Committee feels that Clause 36(3) gives an impression that the employees were debarred from all other
judicial remedies against the decision of the Tribunal.  The Committee is aware that no Act can debar the remedies
available under Articles 226 and 32 of the Constitution.  The Bill also does not intend to do this.  The Committee,
however, recommends that the following explanation may be added in the said Clause for removing the erroneous
impression in this regard.
‘This does not preclude the employees from availing the remedies provided under Articles 226 and 32 of the
Constitution’
Clause 36 (3) may, accordingly, be amended. 
Clause 40
16.       Clause 40, page 12, provides for the final authority in respect of any question regarding election or appointment
of a member of any authority or other body of the University.  The Committee notes that the Bill nowhere mentions
about an elected membership of any authority of the University.  The Committee is of considered opinion that ideally,
the composition/membership of these bodies should have been provided in the Statute itself as was done in the case of
Allahabad University. In view of the fact that the composition of authorities of the university would be subsequently
decided by the university bodies, the Committee wishes to emphasize the need for having elected elements in all the
bodies/authorities of the university.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that suitable mention for the purpose be
made in the Bill at appropriate places.  The Committee further recommends that an enabling provision must be provided
in the Act itself to ensure democratization of various bodies of the University.
Clause 43
17.1     Clause 43, page 13, provides that no suit or other legal proceeding shall lie against any officer or other employee
of the University for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of any of the provisions
of this Act, the Statutes or the Ordinances. 
 
17.2     The Committee feels that the words ‘good faith or intended to be done in pursuance of any of the provisions of
this Act, the Statutes or the Ordinances’ are vague and leave scope for misuse as interpretation of ‘good faith’ could be
subjective.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the ambit of the words ‘good faith or intended to be done in
pursuance of any of the provisions of this Act, the Statutes or the Ordinances’ may be spelt out in clear terms. 
Clause 47
18.       Clause 47, page 14, pertains to Transitional Provisions.  The Committee is of the considered opinion that since
the first officers and authorities of the university are to be appointed or nominated by the Central Government, their
term of offices as provided in transitional provisions should not be long enough. The Committee notes that in some
cases it is five years and in others it is three years.  It, therefore, recommends that the term of office of the first
Chancellor, the first Vice-Chancellor as well as other officers and bodies provided in various sub-clauses of Clause 47
on page 14 should be reduced from five and three years to three and two years respectively. 
THE SCHEDULE
Clauses 2(1) and 2(2) of the Statutes
19.1     Clause 2(1), page 15, of the Statutes provides for the appointment of the                         Vice-Chancellor by the
Visitor from a panel of not less than three persons who shall be recommended by a Committee as constituted under
clause (2).

19.2     Clause 2(2), page 15, provides that the Committee referred to in clause (1) shall consist of three persons, out of
whom two shall be nominated by the Executive Council and one by the Visitor and the nominee of the Visitor shall be
the convenor of the Committee. 
19.3     The Committee finds that the Statute is silent about the background of the persons to be placed on the panel for
appointment as Vice-Chancellor.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the background of the persons who could
be placed on the panel for appointment as Vice-Chancellor of the University may be indicated in the Bill itself.  The
Committee further recommends that a nominee of the Court should also be included in the Selection Committee for
appointment to the post of Vice-Chancellor.
Clauses 9 of the Statutes
20.       Clause 9, page 20, of the Statutes provides for the appointment of a Librarian of the University.  The Committee,
however, notes that the retirement age for the post of Librarian has not been provided for in the Clause.  The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Librarian’s retirement age should also find place in the Bill.
Clause 17 of the Statutes
 
21.       The Committee notes that in case of the ‘Finance Committee’, while its composition has been given, there is no
representation from the University Court in this committee.  The Committee opines that University Court being an
important body should have representation in the Finance Committee. The Committee, therefore, recommends that a
new sub-clause ‘at least one person to be nominated by the Court’ may be added immediately after line 1 of Clause 17
of the Statutes on page 23 of the Bill.
Clause 18(2) of the Statutes
22.1     Clause 18 (2), page 23, provides that a Selection Committee for appointment to the post of Professor shall
consist of the Vice-Chancellor, a nominee of the Visitor, Dean of the Faculty and Head of the Department. 
22.2     The Committee is aware that the Heads of the Department are appointed generally by seniority and rotation.  It
could, therefore, be possible that a Reader happens to be the Head of the Department when the process for appointment
to the post of Professor is underway.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the words ‘if he is a professor’ may
be appended to (ii) of Column 2 of Table against the heading ‘Professor’.
Clause 30(1) of the Statutes
23.1     Clause 30(1), page 27, provides that all powers relating to the maintenance of discipline and disciplinary action
in relation to the students of the University shall vest in the Vice-Chancellor.
23.2     Clause 37(1), page 12, of the principal Act provides that any student or candidate for an examination whose
name has been removed from the rolls of the University by the orders of the Vice-Chancellor, Discipline Committee or
Examination Committee, as the case may be, and who has been debarred from appearing at the examinations of the
University for more than one year, may, within ten days of the date of receipt of such orders or copy of such resolution
by him, appeal to the Executive Council and the Executive Council may confirm, modify and reverse the decision of the
Vice-Chancellor or the Committee, as the case may be. 
23.3     The Committee feels that the provisions of Clause 30(1) of the Statutes and Clause 37(1) of the Principal Act
appear to be contradictory. 
23.4     The Committee, therefore, recommends that the provisions of the Clauses may be suitably re-drafted to remove
the inherent contradictions, if any. 
Clause 40(1) of Statutes
24.       The Committee is of considered opinion that the Act must provide for elected representation of students,
teachers and non-teaching staff in all authoritative bodies of the University and ensure their right to form associations. 
However, the Committee found no such provision for students.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the words
‘two elected representatives of students’ should find place in the constitution of the Student Council and Clause 40 on
page 30 be re-drafted accordingly.
25.       The Committee adopts the remaining clauses of the Bill without any amendments.
26.       The enacting formula and the title are adopted with consequential changes.
27.       The Committee recommends that the Bill may be passed after incorporating the amendments/additions suggested
by it. 
28.       The Committee would like the Department to submit a note with reasons on the recommendations/suggestions,
which could not be incorporated in the Bill.
